subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu support automatic group-sender agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, quota/lifecycle, and memory boundaries become the public contract?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses channel routing, durable agent creation, per-agent skills/config, memory isolation, authorization, and resource governance, so code inspection cannot choose the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Design generic opt-in contract first
options.body: Define the shared identity-to-agent, memory, authorization, TTL/quota, and admin surfaces before adding Feishu-specific group provisioning.

options.title: Keep explicit subagents only
options.body: Continue using group session scopes and explicit thread-bound subagent spawning, and leave per-deployment auto-provisioning to custom plugins or gateway policy.

options.title: Prototype Feishu-only behind a gate
options.body: Allow a narrowly gated Feishu experiment with no default behavior change, but require later migration into a generic channel/plugin contract before broad support.

recommendation.title: Design generic opt-in contract first
recommendation.body: Define the shared identity-to-agent, memory, authorization, TTL/quota, and admin surfaces before adding Feishu-specific group provisioning.

likelyOwner.reason: m1heng is the listed Feishu plugin contact and was pulled into the issue timeline, so they are the best available owner for the Feishu-side product direction with core/security reviewers involved.
